sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin, and I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即便是在我还在夜店用黑胶唱片当DJ的年代，你每天晚上都要带上300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 然后把DJ台变成一个活生生的、快闪式的博物馆，陈列着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, any day now, Senate Republicans will present a vision for overhauling health care that could take insurance away from millions and millions of Americans.
sentences.zh: 今天，或者就在这几天，参议院共和党人将提出一项医疗保健改革方案，该方案可能会让数百万美国人失去保险。

sentences.en: And very few people, not even many Republicans, know what's in the bill.
sentences.zh: 而且很少有人，甚至连许多共和党人自己，都不知道法案里写了什么。

sentences.en: Why Senate leaders are crafting the most important legislation of the Trump presidency in secret.
sentences.zh: 为什么参议院领导人要秘密制定特朗普总统任期内最重要的立法？

sentences.en: It's Monday, June 19th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月19日，星期一。

sentences.en: Let me ask you about, domestically, the issue of health care.
sentences.zh: 让我问问你关于国内医疗保健的问题。

sentences.en: Your Republican colleague, Senator Ron Johnson, said, I want to know exactly what's in the Senate bill.
sentences.zh: 你的共和党同事罗恩·约翰逊参议员说：“我想确切知道参议院法案里有什么。”

sentences.en: It's not a good process.
sentences.zh: 这个流程不太好。

sentences.en: What's your assessment of the process of evaluating health care in the Senate?
sentences.zh: 你对参议院评估医疗保健的流程有什么评价？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's always tough because it's difficult to put something like this together, you know, in front of every camera in the world.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这总是很棘手，因为要在全世界的镜头前把这种事情搞定是很困难的，你知道的。

sentences.en: But ultimately, every camera in the world is going to have to see what's in it, and we're going to have to have plenty of time to debate it.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，全世界的镜头迟早都要看到里面的内容，我们也必须有足够的时间来辩论它。

sentences.en: Carl Hulse, what are the conditions under which Senate Republicans are now writing their health care bill?
sentences.zh: 卡尔·赫尔斯，参议院共和党人现在是在什么样的情况下起草他们的医改法案的？

sentences.en: Give us the scene.
sentences.zh: 给我们描述一下现场情况。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, some of the top Republicans are working behind closed doors, quite honestly, to try and come up with something that can get the magic 50 votes, you know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，一些共和党高层确实是在闭门造车，说实话，他们试图拿出一份能凑齐那关键50票的方案，你知道的。

sentences.en: And it's a question of, like, really sensitively turning the dials to try and get one vote here without losing a vote there.
sentences.zh: 这就像是在非常谨慎地拨动旋钮，试图在这里争取到一票，同时又不失去另一票。

sentences.en: But they're doing it in private, and there's a really good reason for that.
sentences.zh: 但他们是在私下里做这件事，而且这背后有一个非常充分的理由。

sentences.en: Well, what is the reason?
sentences.zh: 那么，理由是什么？

sentences.en: They don't want anyone to know what's in their bill.
sentences.zh: 他们不想让任何人知道法案里写了什么。

sentences.en: Well, first of all, tell me what you mean when you say doing it in private and behind closed doors.
sentences.zh: 好吧，首先，告诉我当你提到“私下里”和“闭门造车”时是什么意思。

sentences.en: What does that actually look like?
sentences.zh: 那实际上是什么样子的？

sentences.en: Well, they talk, you know, they have lunches regularly, and those lunches are always private.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们会交谈，你知道，他们经常一起吃午餐，而那些午餐总是私下的。

sentences.en: But there are also Republicans right now who aren't happy with this.
sentences.zh: 但现在也有共和党人对此感到不满。

sentences.en: It's not just the Democrats who are clamoring.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是民主党人在大声疾呼。

sentences.en: We've begun to hear from Lisa Murkowski of Alaska.
sentences.zh: 我们已经开始听到来自阿拉斯加州的丽莎·穆尔科斯基的声音了。

sentences.en: If I'm not going to see a bill before we have a vote on it, that's just not a good way to handle something that is as significant and important as health care.
sentences.zh: “如果我在投票前看不到法案，那对于处理像医疗保健这样重大且重要的事情来说，绝不是一个好的方式。”

sentences.en: Some of the other members are saying, hey, we don't know what's in this either.
sentences.zh: 其他一些议员也在说：“嘿，我们也不知道这里面有什么。”

sentences.en: We need to know what's in it.
sentences.zh: “我们需要知道里面写了什么。”

sentences.en: The Senate is not a place where you can just cook up something behind closed doors and rush it for a vote on the floor.
sentences.zh: 参议院不是一个你可以随便在闭门会议中炮制出什么东西，然后就匆忙进行投票的地方。

sentences.en: There's just, especially on an issue like this.
sentences.zh: 尤其是对于这样一个议题，更是如此。

sentences.en: Carl, how many senators are we talking about here when we talk about the group of people who are doing this?
sentences.zh: 卡尔，当我们谈论这群正在做这件事的人时，我们指的是多少位参议员？

sentences.en: If you ask Mitch McConnell, he would say all 52 Republicans have a voice.
sentences.zh: 如果你去问米奇·麦康奈尔，他会说所有52位共和党人都有发言权。

sentences.en: Nobody's hiding the ball here.
sentences.zh: 这里没有人搞猫腻。

sentences.en: You're free to ask anybody anything.
sentences.zh: 你可以自由地问任何人任何问题。

sentences.en: I think it changes from day to day and depends on the issue.
sentences.zh: 我认为这每天都在变，取决于具体议题。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, it's going to be decided honestly by Mitch McConnell and a couple of other people and his staff.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，这最终还是由米奇·麦康奈尔、其他几个人以及他的幕僚来决定的。

sentences.en: They're going to say, OK, we're at a place.
sentences.zh: 他们会说：“好了，我们达成一致了。”

sentences.en: We've got the votes and we can go forward.
sentences.zh: “我们已经凑够了票数，可以推进了。”

sentences.en: How does this compare to how a typical piece of legislation is drafted in the United States Senate?
sentences.zh: 这与美国参议院起草典型立法的方式相比如何？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, typically, I always refer to the old schoolhouse rock.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，通常情况下，我总是会提到那个老派的《校园摇滚》（Schoolhouse Rock）。

sentences.en: I'm just a bill up on Capitol Hill, right?
sentences.zh: “我只是国会山上的一个法案，对吧？”

sentences.en: Well, now I'm stuck in committee and I'll sit here and wait while a few key congressmen discuss and debate.
sentences.zh: “好吧，现在我被困在委员会里了，我得坐在这里等，同时几个关键的国会议员在讨论和辩论。”

sentences.en: I mean, you would have committee hearings, you would have markups on various proposals, you would have coalitions come in and talk,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你本该有委员会听证会，会对各种提案进行修订，会有联盟进来讨论，

sentences.en: you would have a chance for people to weigh in and alter this.
sentences.zh: 你会有机会让人们发表意见并修改它。

sentences.en: Now, Claire McCaskill raised a big ruckus at a finance committee meeting.
sentences.zh: 现在，克莱尔·麦卡斯基尔在财政委员会会议上闹出了很大的动静。

sentences.en: So my first question that I would make of the chair is, will we have a hearing on the health care proposal?
sentences.zh: “所以我向主席提出的第一个问题是，我们会就医疗保健提案举行听证会吗？”

sentences.en: Will we?
sentences.zh: “会吗？”

sentences.en: Yes.
Pressing Orrin Hatch saying, hey, are we going to actually have a hearing on this bill?
sentences.zh: 她逼问奥林·哈奇说：“嘿，我们真的要就这个法案举行听证会吗？”

sentences.en: We would really like to hear what's in there.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很想知道里面写了什么。

sentences.en: We don't even know.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至都不知道。

sentences.en: We have no idea what's being proposed.
sentences.zh: 我们完全不知道正在提议什么。

sentences.en: There's a group of guys in a back room somewhere that are making these decisions.
sentences.zh: 有一群人在某个密室里做这些决定。

sentences.en: There were no hearings in the House.
sentences.zh: 众议院那边也没有举行听证会。

sentences.en: So, yeah, this is nothing like a normal bill.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这和正常的法案完全不同。

sentences.en: It's very unusual.
sentences.zh: 这非常不寻常。

sentences.en: So what we're talking about here is that basically one day Republicans are going to emerge with a more or less fully formed bill,
sentences.zh: 所以我们在这里讨论的是，基本上共和党人某天会拿出一份或多或少已经成型的法案，

sentences.en: whereas typically there's all sorts of public hearings and debate and back and forth and conversations.
sentences.zh: 而通常情况下，会有各种公开听证会、辩论以及来回的沟通。

sentences.en: Yeah, certainly on something of this magnitude.
sentences.zh: 是的，特别是在这种量级的议题上。

sentences.en: I mean Republicans inserted quite a few amendments actually into the Affordable Care Act during the process.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，共和党人在《平价医疗法案》的过程中实际上插入了不少修正案。

sentences.en: People forget about that.
sentences.zh: 人们都忘了这一点。

sentences.en: But there were, you know, hearings forever on that.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，当时有没完没了的听证会。

sentences.en: And Republicans did have a chance to weigh in, an actual pretty considerable chance really.
sentences.zh: 共和党人确实有机会发表意见，而且说实话，那是一个相当可观的机会。

sentences.en: So you said the Republicans who are leading this don't want anyone to know what's in this bill.
sentences.zh: 所以你说领导这件事的共和党人不想让任何人知道法案里有什么。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Well, because then it comes under attack and it gives the opposition groups plenty of time to line up their arguments against it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为一旦公开，它就会受到攻击，这给了反对派团体充足的时间来组织反对它的论点。

sentences.en: It even gives Republicans who may be willing in the end to go along with the time to push for their changes.
sentences.zh: 它甚至给了那些最终可能愿意支持的共和党人时间去推动他们想要的修改。

sentences.en: This is going to be such a delicate product when it's done, right?
sentences.zh: 当它完成时，这将是一个非常脆弱的产品，对吧？

sentences.en: If you have a little tinkering one direction or the other, you're going to lose votes and maybe lose your majority.
sentences.zh: 如果你往任何一个方向稍微修补一下，你就会失去选票，甚至可能失去多数席位。

sentences.en: So they're hoping to come up with something, get it out there, vote on it, and then see what happens with the House.
sentences.zh: 所以他们希望能拿出一个方案，发布出来，投票通过，然后看看众议院那边会发生什么。

sentences.en: But the more that's public about it, the more that people can line up against various provisions.
sentences.zh: 但关于它的公开信息越多，人们就越能针对各项条款进行反对。

sentences.en: And this is a bill that directly affects so many people that the consequences are very real for them.
sentences.zh: 这是一个直接影响到这么多人的法案，对他们来说后果是非常现实的。

sentences.en: So they tend to weigh in.
sentences.zh: 所以他们倾向于发表意见。

sentences.en: And Congress is not usually in the business of taking away benefits from people.
sentences.zh: 而且国会通常不会做那种剥夺民众福利的事情。

sentences.en: And it makes it really, really politically charged.
sentences.zh: 这让它在政治上变得非常、非常敏感。

sentences.en: And so they're leery of that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对此心存顾虑。

sentences.en: So what do we think is likely to be most controversial in this bill?
sentences.zh: 那么我们认为这个法案中最具争议的内容可能是什么？

sentences.en: Do you have a sense of that?
sentences.zh: 你对此有什么感觉吗？

sentences.en: You know, it's hard to say as even some of the Republican senators say, well, we can't say anything because we don't know what's in the bill ourselves.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很难说，因为连一些共和党参议员都说：“好吧，我们什么都不能说，因为我们自己也不知道法案里有什么。”

sentences.en: But we know what the key areas are, how much you can provide sure coverage for pre-existing conditions.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道关键领域是什么，比如对既往症的覆盖能提供多少保障。

sentences.en: How much of the Medicaid expansion do you keep?
sentences.zh: 医疗补助（Medicaid）的扩张保留多少？

sentences.en: I think, you know, it's going to be the points of controversy that we've seen in the past on this.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，这将会是我们过去在这个问题上看到的争议点。

sentences.en: And they're just trying to fine-tune it to the point where they can get 50 votes.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在试图微调它，直到能凑够50票。

sentences.en: That is the goal here.
sentences.zh: 这就是目标。

sentences.en: Just whatever we have to do to assemble a 50-vote-getting machine, that's what we're going to do.
sentences.zh: 无论我们需要做什么来组装一台能拿到50票的机器，我们都会去做。

sentences.en: And we don't want too many people throwing wrenches into the process before we're ready.
sentences.zh: 而且我们不想在准备好之前有太多人来搅局。

sentences.en: And I guess we should remind people of the way this math works.
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该提醒大家这种数学逻辑是如何运作的。

sentences.en: 50 votes is traditionally not enough to get something through the U.S.
sentences.zh: 50票在传统上不足以让某项法案通过美国参议院。

sentences.en: Senate.
sentences.zh: 但当副总统是共和党人，并且他投下决定性的一票时，就可以了。

sentences.en: But when the vice president is a Republican and he's casting the tie-breaking vote, it is.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 而且这也是通过“和解程序”来完成的。

sentences.en: And also this is being done through reconciliation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，通常在参议院，确实需要60票，

sentences.en: I mean, normally in the Senate, really, it takes 60 votes,
sentences.zh: 这正是民主党人在制定《平价医疗法案》时所拥有的巨大优势，他们能够靠自己完成。

sentences.en: which was the great advantage that the Democrats had when they did the Affordable Care Act and were able to do it on their own.
sentences.zh: 他们在参议院曾有短暂的时间拥有60票，这让他们无需共和党人的投票就能通过法案。

sentences.en: They had 60 votes for a brief period in the Senate, and it allowed them to do it without Republican votes.
sentences.zh: 共和党人没有这个条件，所以他们也必须走这个程序，这是另一个真正的难点，因为它被称为“和解程序”。

sentences.en: Republicans don't have that, so they also have to go through this process, which is another real wrinkle because there's only – it's called reconciliation.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们现在陷入细节了。

sentences.en: I know we're down in the weeds here.
sentences.zh: 卡尔，当你提到“和解”这个词时，我脑子里想的是参议院正在字面上试图将他们关于医疗保健的想法与众议院的法案进行“和解”。

sentences.en: Carl, when you say the word reconciliation, in my mind, that means that the Senate is trying to literally reconcile their ideas about health care with this House bill.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 那是——不对吗？

sentences.en: That was – no?
sentences.zh: 不，不。

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 我可以回到——

sentences.en: I could go back to –
sentences.zh: 我们能把我们的理解“和解”一下吗？

sentences.en: Can we please reconcile our understanding?
sentences.zh: 我可以回到——我只是国会山上的一个法案，但我认为那个法案并没有进入和解程序。

sentences.en: I can go back to – I'm just a bill up on Capitol Hill, but I don't think that one actually got into reconciliation.
sentences.zh: 你所说的是以后会发生的“协商委员会”，但“和解”是指将实际的政策和立法与预算数字进行协调。

sentences.en: What you're talking about is what would be a conference committee that would happen later, but reconciling is reconciling the actual policy and legislation with the budget numbers.
sentences.zh: 这就是“和解”在这两件事之间的含义。

sentences.en: That's the reconciliation is between those two things.
sentences.zh: 所以你通过预算设定了这种程序，这就是你正在进行“和解”的内容。

sentences.en: So you set up this kind of process through the budget, and that's what you're reconciling with.
sentences.zh: 此外，有些人倾向于认为这意味着立法者正在让自己“和解”接受它，但这也不是那个意思。

sentences.en: Also, some people tend to think that it means that the lawmakers are reconciling themselves to it, but that doesn't mean that either.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 那么，话虽如此，对于为什么要以这种如此保密的方式进行，有什么令人信服的理由吗？

sentences.en: Well, all that being said, is there a compelling case for why it should be done precisely as it's being done with so much secrecy?
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你不想让人们知道你的法案里有什么并攻击它的话。

sentences.en: Sure, if you don't want people to know what's in your bill and attack it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，在政府事务上，我算是一个政府纯粹主义者或者说是个老实人。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, I'm sort of a government purist or a goody two-shoes guy when it comes to government.
sentences.zh: 我知道这很难想象。

sentences.en: I know that's hard to imagine.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，就像是把它拿出来。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's like put it out there.
sentences.zh: 就它进行辩论。

sentences.en: Have a debate on it.
sentences.zh: 让人们发表意见。

sentences.en: Let people weigh in on it.
sentences.zh: 在议会大厅进行投票。

sentences.en: Have the votes on the floor.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，参议院最近陷入了这样一个循环，每个人都害怕投票。

sentences.en: Or, you know, the Senate has gotten into this cycle recently where everyone is scared to take votes.
sentences.zh: 我一直说，你知道，就直接投票表决吧。

sentences.en: I've always said, you know, just vote on things.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们——

sentences.en: I think that people—
sentences.zh: 你真的会对参议员们这么说吗？

sentences.en: Do you actually say that to senators?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你处于一个独特的位置，能够对他们说这些话。

sentences.en: I mean, you're in the unique position of being able to say that to them.
sentences.zh: 他们接下来会说什么？

sentences.en: What do they say next?
sentences.zh: 我说，你们为什么不直接投票呢？

sentences.en: I say, why don't you just vote?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，很多参议员会说，我们希望我们有更多的票数，民主党人肯定会这么说。

sentences.en: And, you know, a lot of senators will say, we wish we had more votes, and the Democrats would definitely say that.
sentences.zh: 但这个地方已经变得如此党派化，以至于对于这种法案，根本没有这种来回协商的空间。

sentences.en: But the place has become so partisan that there's no room for this kind of back-and-forth negotiation on this kind of bill.
sentences.zh: 而且这绝对不是《校园摇滚》里那种炮制法案的方式，如果我还要回到那个例子的话。

sentences.en: And it's definitely not the way that they cooked it up for Schoolhouse Rock, if I want to keep going back to that one.
sentences.zh: 你是说开国元勋们？

sentences.en: You mean the founders?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，他们实际上在开始时也是秘密会面的，你知道。

sentences.en: Well, you know, they actually met in secret, you know, at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 参议院曾经是一个封闭的机构。

sentences.en: The Senate was a closed body.
sentences.zh: 所以说实话，他们对公开透明也不是那么热衷。

sentences.en: So they weren't all that much for openness either, to tell you the truth.
sentences.zh: 但经过了，你知道，漫长的岁月，它已经发展成了一个更加开放的程序。

sentences.en: But over the, you know, eons here, you know, it's developed into a more open process.
sentences.zh: 国会山上总是有秘密。

sentences.en: There's always secrecy on Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 但对于这种量级的法案来说，这可能确实达到了一个新的高度。

sentences.en: But this is probably a new level, really, for something of this magnitude.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 所以这让我想谈谈希拉里·克林顿。

sentences.en: So this makes me want to talk about Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 我记得在1993年，

sentences.en: And I remember back in 1993,
sentences.zh: 当比尔·克林顿总统要求时任第一夫人希拉里·罗德姆带头改革美国医疗保健系统时，那种感觉相当隐秘。

sentences.en: when President Bill Clinton asked then-First Lady Hillary Rodham to take the lead in overhauling the American health care system in a way that felt pretty secretive.
sentences.zh: 在公开场合，希拉里·克林顿坚决回避了关于如何支付所有费用的棘手问题。

sentences.en: In public, Hillary Clinton has resolutely avoided the hard questions of how to pay for it all.
sentences.zh: “我不会就我们最终会得出什么结论发表任何声明。”

sentences.en: I'm not going to make any statement about exactly where we're going to come out on that.
sentences.zh: 那里面确实有秘密的成分，我认为这让他们吃了苦头。

sentences.en: There were secretive aspects to that, and I think that that blew up on them.
sentences.zh: 希拉里·克林顿知道她必须修复与医疗专业人士的关系，他们仍然对她工作组的秘密行事方式感到不满。

sentences.en: Hillary Clinton knows she must repair relations with health professionals, still upset at the secretive ways of her task force.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在后来伤害了他们。

sentences.en: I think that that hurt them later.
sentences.zh: 人们不确定法案里有什么。

sentences.en: People weren't sure what was in the bill.
sentences.zh: 他们真的不确定发生了什么。

sentences.en: They weren't really sure what was going on.
sentences.zh: 它只是从来没有……它因为自身的重量而崩溃了。

sentences.en: It just never, it sort of collapsed of its own weight.
sentences.zh: 它只是从来没有……它因为自身的重量而崩溃了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So are there similarities between what was derisively known by its critics as Hillary care and what is now somewhat derisively known by its critics as Trump care as it moves its way to the Senate?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于那个被批评者嘲讽为“希拉里医改”的方案，以及现在正送往参议院、同样被批评者嘲讽为“特朗普医改”的方案，两者之间是否存在相似之处？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I think at the time that that was such an expansive topic at that time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我认为在当时，那是一个非常宏大的议题。

sentences.en: It was so new, you know, a federal makeover of the health care system and people weren't exactly sure what was going on.
sentences.zh: 那太新颖了，你知道的，对医疗体系进行联邦层面的彻底改造，人们并不确定到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And I think it scared off members of both sides.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这吓跑了双方的议员。

sentences.en: I think there is a political philosophy that whichever party is the mover or they call it as the instigator on health care always gets a backlash.
sentences.zh: 我认为存在一种政治哲学，即无论哪个党派是医改的推动者，或者他们所称的始作俑者，总是会遭到强烈抵制。

sentences.en: It's because it touches people so directly.
sentences.zh: 这是因为它直接触及了人们的切身利益。

sentences.en: It is super complicated.
sentences.zh: 它极其复杂。

sentences.en: It's hard to address legislatively and it's very easy to criticize.
sentences.zh: 在立法层面很难处理，而且非常容易受到批评。

sentences.en: It's like, this is going to cost too much.
sentences.zh: 就像是，这会花费太多钱。

sentences.en: This is going to deny people something.
sentences.zh: 这会剥夺人们的某些东西。

sentences.en: And, you know, it really hits home with people.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，它真的让人们感同身受。

sentences.en: It's direct.
sentences.zh: 它很直接。

sentences.en: It's one of the things that the government's involved in, you know, that as the death panel debate showed, well, the government's going to be able to decide who lives and who dies.
sentences.zh: 这是政府参与的事务之一，你知道，正如“死亡委员会”辩论所显示的那样，嗯，政府将能够决定谁生谁死。

sentences.en: Now, that wasn't particularly true, but it was a really good message.
sentences.zh: 现在，这并非完全属实，但那确实是一个非常有力的信息。

sentences.en: And it really made it hard for the Democrats to move ahead with Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 而且这确实让民主党人很难推进“奥巴马医改”。

sentences.en: So, Carl, give us a sense of timing here.
sentences.zh: 那么，卡尔，给我们讲讲时间安排吧。

sentences.en: When are we expecting to see this Republican health care bill or do we have no idea because it's a secret?
sentences.zh: 我们预计什么时候能看到这份共和党的医改法案？还是说我们根本不知道，因为它是保密的？

sentences.en: I think the thinking anyway is that they would like to get it out and considered on the floor before going home for the 4th of July.
sentences.zh: 我想目前的想法是，他们希望在7月4日国庆假期休会前将其拿出来并在参议院进行审议。

sentences.en: They've got a lot of things to do.
sentences.zh: 他们有很多事情要做。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So that's very soon.
sentences.zh: 那很快了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: No, I think you're going to see in the next couple of weeks they're either going to get it out, it's going to succeed or it's going to fail.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为在接下来的几周里，你会看到他们要么把它拿出来，要么成功，要么失败。

sentences.en: There are Republicans who will say, let's just vote on it, and if it fails, then we're done with it.
sentences.zh: 有些共和党人会说，我们就表决吧，如果失败了，那我们就此了结。

sentences.en: You know, the Senate Republicans would have been very happy for the House not to pass their bill at all, and they would have never had to do this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，参议院的共和党人本来会很高兴众议院根本不通过他们的法案，这样他们就永远不必处理这件事了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Are you saying that Senate Republicans may be doing this in secret in part because that way if it fails to get enough votes,
sentences.zh: 你是说参议院共和党人可能秘密进行此事，部分原因是这样如果法案未能获得足够票数，

sentences.en: then they haven't gone through this drawn-out public drama around their values and their vision of health care?
sentences.zh: 他们就不必经历围绕其价值观和医改愿景的漫长公开闹剧了吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But also, I mean, it's not like you're not going to know what's in the bill when it's out there being considered.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我的意思是，这并不是说当法案被拿出来审议时，你不会知道里面写了什么。

sentences.en: It's not a black box.
sentences.zh: 它不是一个黑匣子。

sentences.en: You know, people have a chance to take a look at it,
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们有机会去查看它，

sentences.en: but I just think for them they have found that this is the most efficient way to do this and resolve their problem one way or the other.
sentences.zh: 但我只是认为对他们来说，他们发现这是处理此事并以某种方式解决问题的最有效方法。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's secret now, but it's going to get out there, and it'll be an epic showdown.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，现在是保密的，但它最终会公之于众，那将是一场史诗般的对决。

sentences.en: Trust me.
sentences.zh: 相信我。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Because you're basically the parliamentarian of the Senate, here's what I want to ask you.
sentences.zh: 因为你基本上是参议院的议事规则专家，我想问你这个问题。

sentences.en: How does this actually work?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么运作的？

sentences.en: It comes out, this piece of legislation, who controls how quickly it comes to a vote, and what's the time between it coming out and the vote?
sentences.zh: 这份立法草案出炉后，谁来控制它多快进入表决程序？从出炉到表决之间的时间间隔是多久？

sentences.en: Well, I don't think you're going to be able to get away with announcing it one night and then passing it the next day,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不认为你能蒙混过关，一天晚上宣布，第二天就通过，

sentences.en: although I've seen both parties try and do things like that in Congress over the years.
sentences.zh: 尽管多年来我见过两党在国会都尝试过类似的事情。

sentences.en: Whether it's an appropriate amount of time,
sentences.zh: 至于这是否是合适的时间长度，

sentences.en: no one's going to agree with that because the Democrats think they should have been having hearings and votes and amendments and all sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 没人会同意这一点，因为民主党人认为他们本应该进行听证、表决、修正案以及各种各样的程序。

sentences.en: But it'll take a matter of days for this to play out, but it's not going to be satisfactory to anyone.
sentences.zh: 但这需要几天时间来走完流程，不过这不会让任何人满意。

sentences.en: Trust me on that one as well.
sentences.zh: 这一点也请相信我。

sentences.en: They are going to really rail about the way this bill was assembled.
sentences.zh: 他们真的会大肆抨击这项法案的起草方式。

sentences.en: That's going to be one of their major lines of attack.
sentences.zh: 那将是他们主要的攻击点之一。

sentences.en: Carl, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 卡尔，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Michael, I'm happy to talk health care with you.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，很高兴和你谈论医改。

sentences.en: You really are.
sentences.zh: 你确实很高兴。

sentences.en: I am.
sentences.zh: 我是。

sentences.en: I'm totally happy.
sentences.zh: 我完全很高兴。

sentences.en: Thanks, Carl.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，卡尔。

sentences.en: See you later.
sentences.zh: 回头见。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilron Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔隆·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过NYTimes.com直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，阅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: Has the special counsel, Robert Mueller, formally notified the president that he is under investigation?
sentences.zh: 特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒是否已正式通知总统他正在接受调查？

sentences.en: On Sunday, a lawyer for President Trump, Jay Sekulow, went on Fox News to face questions from Chris Wallace.
sentences.zh: 周日，特朗普总统的律师杰伊·塞库洛上了福克斯新闻，接受克里斯·华莱士的质询。

sentences.en: Two days earlier,
sentences.zh: 两天前，

sentences.en: the president had for the first time said publicly that he's the subject of an investigation by the special counsel looking into Russian meddling in the 2016 election.
sentences.zh: 总统首次公开表示，他是特别检察官调查2016年大选俄罗斯干预事件的对象。

sentences.en: The president has not been notified by anyone that he's under investigation.
sentences.zh: 总统没有收到任何人关于他正在接受调查的通知。

sentences.en: That tweet, Chris, was in response to the Washington Post story that alleged that five unnamed sources, anonymous sources, leaked to the Washington Post,
sentences.zh: 那条推文，克里斯，是为了回应《华盛顿邮报》的报道，该报道声称有五个未具名的消息来源，匿名消息来源，向《华盛顿邮报》泄露了，

sentences.en: that the president was in fact under investigation.
sentences.zh: 总统实际上正在接受调查。

sentences.en: So that tweet was in response to that.
sentences.zh: 所以那条推文是为了回应那个报道。

sentences.en: There's been no notification of any investigation.
sentences.zh: 没有任何关于调查的通知。

sentences.en: Nothing's changed since James Comey said the president was not a target or a subject of investigation.
sentences.zh: 自从詹姆斯·科米说总统不是调查的目标或对象以来，什么都没有改变。

sentences.en: Nothing's changed.
sentences.zh: 什么都没有改变。

sentences.en: But in the same interview with Chris Wallace, Sekulow said this.
sentences.zh: 但在接受克里斯·华莱士的同一次采访中，塞库洛说了这样的话。

sentences.en: And now he's being investigated by the Department of Justice because the special counsel under the special counsel regulations reports still to the Department of Justice,
sentences.zh: 现在他正受到司法部的调查，因为特别检察官根据特别检察官条例仍然向司法部报告，

sentences.en: not an independent counsel.
sentences.zh: 而不是一个独立的检察官。

sentences.en: So he's being investigated for taking the action that the attorney general, deputy attorney general, recommended him to take by the agency who recommended the termination.
sentences.zh: 所以他因为采取了司法部长、副司法部长建议他采取的行动，而受到建议解雇他的机构的调查。

sentences.en: Wallace reminded Sekulow of what he just said.
sentences.zh: 华莱士提醒塞库洛他刚才说了什么。

sentences.en: First of all, you've now said that he is being investigated after saying that you didn't know you just said that you just said that he's being investigated.
sentences.zh: 首先，你刚才说他正在接受调查，而在那之前你说你不知道，你刚刚确实说了他正在接受调查。

sentences.en: No, Chris, I said that the invent anything.
sentences.zh: 不，克里斯，我说的是……我没编造任何东西。

sentences.en: Let me be crystal clear.
sentences.zh: 让我说得非常清楚。

sentences.en: So you completely understand we have not received nor are we aware of any investigation of the president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 为了让你完全理解，我们没有收到，也不知晓任何针对美国总统的调查。

sentences.en: So you just said two times that on Friday, the president had tweeted, quote,
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才两次说，周五总统发推文说，引用：

sentences.en: I am being investigated for firing the FBI director by the man who told me to fire the FBI director, Witch Hunt.
sentences.zh: “我因为解雇联邦调查局局长而受到调查，调查我的人正是告诉我解雇联邦调查局局长的人，猎巫行动。”

sentences.en: On Sunday, Sekulow said the president had been constrained by Twitter.
sentences.zh: 周日，塞库洛说总统受到了推特的限制。

sentences.en: There's a limitation on Twitter, as we all know, he said.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所知，推特有字数限制，他说。

sentences.en: And the president has a very effective utilization of social media.
sentences.zh: 而且总统对社交媒体的使用非常有效。

sentences.en: And there were rulings in two court cases we told you about on Friday.
sentences.zh: 周五我们告诉过你们两起法庭案件的裁决。

sentences.en: In Norristown, Pennsylvania, the judge in the Bill Cosby trial declared a mistrial after a jury of seven men and five women,
sentences.zh: 在宾夕法尼亚州诺里斯敦，比尔·科斯比审判案的法官在由七名男性和五名女性组成的陪审团宣布他们无法就科斯比是否性侵了安德烈亚·康斯坦达成一致后，宣布审判无效，

sentences.en: 10 of them white, two of them black, declared they were hopelessly deadlocked about whether Cosby had sexually assaulted Andrea Constant,
sentences.zh: 其中10名白人，2名黑人，他们表示在科斯比是否性侵安德烈亚·康斯坦的问题上陷入了彻底的僵局，

sentences.en: one of more than 40 women who have accused him of sexual assault.
sentences.zh: 她是40多名指控他性侵的女性之一。

sentences.en: We will evaluate and review our case.
sentences.zh: 我们将评估和审查我们的案件。

sentences.en: We will take a hard look at everything involved, and then we will retry it.
sentences.zh: 我们将认真审视所涉及的一切，然后我们将重审此案。

sentences.en: As I said in court, our plan is to move this case forward as soon as possible.
sentences.zh: 正如我在法庭上所说，我们的计划是尽快推进此案。

sentences.en: We have one victim.
sentences.zh: 我们有一名受害者。

sentences.en: We have Andrea Constant.
sentences.zh: 我们有安德烈亚·康斯坦。

sentences.en: She has shown such courage through this, and I think I share our thoughts on her.
sentences.zh: 她在此过程中展现了极大的勇气，我想我代表我们表达对她的想法。

sentences.en: We're just in awe of what she has done.
sentences.zh: 我们对她的所作所为感到敬佩。

sentences.en: And in Taunton, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 在马萨诸塞州汤顿。

sentences.en: Scarlet police stand.
sentences.zh: 斯卡利警官请起立。

sentences.en: This court, having reviewed the evidence and applied the law thereto, now finds you guilty.
sentences.zh: 本庭在审查了证据并适用相关法律后，现裁定你有罪。

sentences.en: A judge convicted 20-year-old Michelle Carter of involuntary manslaughter in the suicide of Conrad Roy
sentences.zh: 一名法官裁定20岁的米歇尔·卡特在康拉德·罗伊自杀案中犯有过失杀人罪，

sentences.en: after concluding that Carter had told Roy over the phone to get back into the cab of his pickup truck
sentences.zh: 结论是卡特在电话中告诉罗伊回到他的皮卡车驾驶室里，

sentences.en: and then listen to him die from carbon monoxide poisoning without trying to help.
sentences.zh: 然后听着他死于一氧化碳中毒而没有试图提供帮助。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》到此结束。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: I'll be going on vacation starting tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我从明天开始休假。

sentences.en: My colleague Caitlin Dickerson will be hosting while I'm away.
sentences.zh: 我不在期间，我的同事凯特琳·迪克森将担任主持。

sentences.en: See you soon.
sentences.zh: 回头见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在我和莎拉·凯尼格主持的最新一期《地铁》节目中，讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。
